title: SeqLen Mosaic Packer — attention-fission microbatch shaping with kernel hinting
creator: Ava Marshall
description: Goal: Reduce wasted padding and improve end-to-end throughput for heterogeneous request mixes by introducing a "mosaic" seqlen packing algorithm combined with an attention-fission optimization and explicit kernel-hint annotations on batches. The mosaic packer groups requests into mixed-length micro-batches that maximize GPU kernel utilization while bounding decode tail latency. Attention-fission separates attention computation into a short-context dense pass and a long-context sparse pass so that we can schedule the most efficient kernels per subtask.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end token cost reduction >= 18% on mixed production traffic (measured over 48h rolling window) compared to current length-bucketing baseline
2) 95th percentile decode latency increase <= 8% for latency-sensitive short requests under 200ms baseline
3) Throughput (tokens/sec) improvement >= 12% for baseline seqlen distribution with 10% long tails
4) No regressions on stable QA evals and model output fidelity (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR where applicable)
5) CI integration tests for kernel-hint metadata and attention-fission paths pass on x86+NVIDIA CI runners
design_decisions: Use a lightweight online clustering heuristic (mosaic) instead of heavy hierarchical clustering to keep scheduling overhead < 0.5ms per request

Favor packing mixes of short and medium sequences into a single micro-batch to increase kernel occupancy while limiting pad inflation — long requests are isolated when they exceed a tunable footprint threshold
Implement attention-fission at the runtime level so model-agnostic: split attention into two kernel calls (dense_short_ctx + sparse_long_ctx) with optional KV cache merging
Attach kernel-hint tags to batch metadata (e.g., kernel:fast-dense, kernel:sparse-merge) to allow the executor to pick precompiled kernels without model introspection
tradeoffs: Pros: better utilization and measurable token cost reduction; allows specialized kernels to shine on subparts of the work
Cons: increased scheduler complexity and slightly more bookkeeping for KV cache merging across fissioned attention passes
Edge case: Synthetic traffic with uniformly long sequences may see no benefit; algorithm degrades gracefully to current bucketing
Operational: New telemetry required to explain per-request packing decisions and to debug correctness when fissioned attention is enabled
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype mosaic packer in runtime simulator using production request traces; evaluate pad savings and packing overhead
Week 2: Implement attention-fission kernel API and add kernel-hint metadata on batch objects; add unit tests for KV cache merging semantics
Week 3: Integrate mosaic packer into prefill scheduler path (prefill-time packing) and add a decode-time fallback policy
Week 4: Run A/B on staging with telemetry dashboards + validate acceptance criteria; iterate tuning knobs (mosaic size, long-request threshold)
Week 5: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic on runtime-1.22; monitor cost/latency, then incrementally ramp
benchmarks: Local simulator results (mixed trace A): pad tokens reduced by 21%, tokens/sec +14%, 95p decode latency +5%
Cluster CI (small GPU pool): end-to-end cost/QPS model projection shows ~15% unit-cost reduction for typical PLG workload
Microbench kernel latency: dense_short_ctx kernel ~25% faster than baseline full-attn on short sequences; sparse_long_ctx latency varies with sparsity config
